holidays.name: National Tortilla Chip Day
holidays.description: A crunchy celebration of the triangular snack that makes salsa, guacamole, and queso possible. Fans mark the day by dipping, crunching, and debating the ideal chip-to-dip ratio.
holidays.origin: The tortilla chip is widely credited to Rebecca Webb Carranza, who ran a Los Angeles tortilla factory in the late 1940s and began selling bags of misshapen tortilla scraps that had been fried. The commemorative day is an informal food observance popularized through food-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Rebecca Webb Carranza's family business, El Zarape Tortilla Factory, reportedly sold the chips for about a dime a bag, and her scrap-saving idea helped popularize the snack across the U.S.

holidays.name: World Bartender Day
holidays.description: A toast to the people who pour, shake, stir, and listen to your life stories at the bar. Patrons are encouraged to tip well, order something creative, and appreciate the craft of mixology.
holidays.origin: It is an informal industry observance that grew out of the modern cocktail and hospitality community, aimed at recognizing the skill and hard work behind the bar.
holidays.funFact: Professional bartenders sometimes train to pour precise measures by counting in their heads, and flair competitions have bartenders juggling bottles and shakers like circus performers.

holidays.name: National Skip the Straw Day
holidays.description: A day for sipping directly from the glass and giving single-use plastic straws a break. It encourages people to rethink small habits that add up to a lot of waste.
holidays.origin: The observance arose from the broader anti-plastic movement of the 2010s, which gained momentum after viral awareness campaigns about plastic straws and marine pollution.
holidays.funFact: Drinking straws date back thousands of years, and the ancient Sumerians reportedly used gold and lapis lazuli straws to sip beer.

holidays.name: Flag Day in Mexico (Día de la Bandera)
holidays.description: A patriotic celebration in which Mexicans honor their green, white, and red flag with ceremonies, parades in schools, and salutes to the national eagle emblem.
holidays.origin: The day was established in 1937 by President Lázaro Cárdenas. It commemorates the Plan of Iguala, which was proclaimed in 1821 and introduced the tricolor design during the Mexican War of Independence.
holidays.funFact: The Mexican flag features an eagle perched on a cactus devouring a snake, referencing the Aztec legend of the founding of Tenochtitlan.

holidays.name: Estonian Independence Day
holidays.description: A national celebration featuring concerts, military parades, flag-raisings, and a presidential reception for guests dressed in their finest, marking Estonia's declaration of independence.
holidays.origin: Estonia declared independence from Russia on February 24, 1918, a day before German forces arrived, and the date has been commemorated as the nation's birthday ever since.
holidays.funFact: Estonia is known as one of the most digitally advanced countries in the world and pioneered e-residency, letting people around the globe start a business there online.
